clue.text: Flag for second base

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second, as in units of time
lowdown as an adjective means mean or despicable, just as base does

explanation.surface: A signal flag is run up to mark second base on a ball field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb, meaning to tire or lose pace; 'base' is the adjective meaning low-minded, not a ballpark bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire and lose speed, which is to ease off the pace.

clue.text: Issue needs growth as source of future profit

parts.note: seed means offspring or issue, as in the Bible
corn is a growth, the hard patch on a foot

explanation.surface: A matter needing development to pay off later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a topic but means offspring; 'growth' is a hard patch on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedcorn is grain kept back for sowing, and figuratively anything held back to yield later gain.

clue.text: Gap's established an opportunity

definitions.meaning: a space or aperture in something
a chance, such as a job vacancy

explanation.surface: A vacancy is described as a real chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a space through which one passes and a chance to advance share the word for a breach or vacancy.

clue.text: Exercise baboon

definitions.meaning: a West African monkey related to the mandrill

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both repetitive training practice and a West African ape-like monkey.

clue.text: Blessing spring for luck

definitions.meaning: wishing someone well is giving them a blessing
a well into which coins are thrown while making a wish

explanation.surface: A fountain is thought to bring good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoping for someone's good fortune is a benediction, and the same phrase names a fountain for coin-tossing wishes.

clue.text: Man is one, though poet would disagree

definitions.text: Man is one, though poet would disagree

parts.words: Man is one, though poet would disagree
parts.note: the Isle of Man is a piece of land in the sea, while John Donne wrote that no man is one

explanation.surface: A claim about mankind that a poet would dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea; John Donne's famous line 'No man is an island' supplies the poet who would disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is land surrounded by sea, though Donne's sermon denies that any person is cut off like that.

clue.text: Estranged peer, sour; with touch of hubris may appear as such

definitions.text: Estranged peer, sour; with touch of hubris may appear as such

indicators.note: estranged means set apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order
a touch is just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bitter, alienated aristocrat with a dash of arrogance may become a comic-book figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PEER SOUR plus H, the first letter of 'hubris', gives the answer; the whole clue describes such a caped figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic-book heroes often start as wronged, embittered outsiders and carry a streak of arrogance.

clue.text: Misfit abnormally deficient at regular intervals

indicators.note: deficient at intervals says letters are lost from the word at points along its length

explanation.surface: An outsider is oddly lacking at set times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient at regular intervals' removes B, R and L from ABNORMALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something that does not fit the pattern, an oddity or exception.

clue.text: Hate getting low pass grades on examination

parts.note: D and E are low passing grades in exams
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A student loathes scraping through a test with poor marks.
explanation.walkthrough: D and E are low pass grades in British school exams such as A levels.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is to despise it.

clue.text: Run round when chasing English poet

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the English one
round says one word goes around another

parts.note: to leg it is slang for running off
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An English poet is pursued as he runs round a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is slang 'leg it', and 'round' wraps that verb about the word for 'when'; 'chasing' sets the result behind the English letter. An elegiast need not be English: that word only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegiast is a writer of elegies, mournful verses, so a kind of versifier.

clue.text: Shoot rector in jet

indicators.note: in places the clergyman's letter inside the jet of water

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid

explanation.surface: Someone shoots a vicar with a water jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a verb of attack but is the noun for new growth on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A new growth from a plant or seed is a shoot.

clue.text: Rise after cold, a mild one

indicators.note: after puts the rise behind the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A temperature rise follows a spell of cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in the definition refers back to 'cold': a slight cold, the illness, is the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight feverish cold with shivering is commonly called catching a chill.

clue.text: All-time greats riding smart limo

indicators.note: riding about, the letters of the two words are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Legends of the game ride in a fancy limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riding' signals the anagram of SMART LIMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortals are figures whose fame lasts for ever, the greatest of all time.

clue.text: Spy Victoria, say, in act of assault

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
Victoria is a London railway terminus, an example of a station

explanation.surface: A spy is caught attacking at a London terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a major London railway station; 'say' signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Molestation is harassment or physical interference with someone.

clue.text: Bad eggs, real loury, appear here

definitions.text: Bad eggs, real loury, appear here

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the following words are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Villains, glowering darkly, are pictured in a mugshot collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' signals the anagram of EGGS REAL LOURY; 'loury' means frowning or gloomy. The whole clue also describes the place: bad eggs appear in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A police collection of photographs of known criminals is where scoundrels' faces appear.

clue.text: What divides Iraq: the USA, pre getting disentangled

indicators.note: disentangled suggests the letters are untangled and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Before American involvement, Iraq is split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting disentangled' signals the anagram of THE USA PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Mesopotamian river flows through Iraq from north-west to south-east, cutting the country.

clue.text: Riddle set by teacher after end of class

indicators.note: after shows the trainer follows the end letter
end of picks out the final letter of the word

parts.note: a trainer is one who teaches skills

explanation.surface: A teacher sets a puzzle once the lesson ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large sieve, and a sieve is also called a strainer.

clue.text: Train Greek scholar as an artist

parts.note: an express is a fast train
Ion is a Greek, the legendary ancestor of the Ionians and the rhapsode in Plato's dialogue
-ist is the suffix for a specialist or student of a subject

explanation.surface: Someone trains a Greek academic to become a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb but is the fast railway service.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionist is a painter of the early twentieth-century movement that distorted form to convey emotion.

clue.text: Golfer and actor in studio

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A golfer and an actor appear at a film studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree is home to famous film and TV studios north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree, in Hertfordshire, is a town known for its film and television studios.

clue.text: Apparent understanding

definitions.meaning: visible, as two words meaning within view
perception or grasp of a matter

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means within view, so visible; as one word it means deep perception.

clue.text: Rate vehicle goes over hump

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the hump and a pet are both a fit of sulking

explanation.surface: A vehicle's speed is checked over a speed hump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' is the verb to scold; 'hump' is British for a sulk, as in 'get the hump'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to summon and reprimand them, which is what rating someone means.

clue.text: What's accommodating to a marsupial, not pom?

definitions.text: What's accommodating to a marsupial, not pom?

parts.words: What's accommodating to a marsupial, not pom?
parts.note: a country that is home to kangaroos and koalas, where an English immigrant is mocked as a pom

explanation.surface: A riddle about which place welcomes a pouched mammal but not an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pom' is Antipodean slang for an English person; the country welcomes its native pouched animals but famously teases the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Most of the world's pouched mammals live in this southern continent-country, where Englishmen are nicknamed poms.

clue.text: Infatuation with a governor

parts.note: a pash is British slang for a crush or infatuation

explanation.surface: Someone has a crush on a state governor.
explanation.walkthrough: PASH is dated British schoolgirl slang for a crush.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman provincial governor or official.

clue.text: Vegetable showing sign of life

definitions.meaning: edible seeds such as lentils and beans
the throb of blood in an artery

explanation.surface: A vegetable displays signs of being alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both edible legume seeds and the heartbeat felt at the wrist.

clue.text: Filibuster sets one in inconsequential talk

indicators.note: in shows the numeral is set inside the chatter

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on idly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A politician talking out a bill puts someone into idle chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filibuster' suggests the political talking-out tactic, but its old sense is a freebooter or buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibuster in its original sense was a freebooting adventurer who plundered, a sea robber.

clue.text: Girl collects 1000 for sacked radio reporter

indicators.note: collects shows the girl's name gathering the other letter inside it

parts.note: Gillian is a girl's name
G stands for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A young woman raises a thousand for a journalist who lost his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Gilligan was the BBC radio reporter whose 2003 Iraq dossier story led to his resignation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Gilligan was the BBC Today programme correspondent who left after the Hutton inquiry.

clue.text: Fly with some of jet-set's elite

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An insect mingles with the glamorous rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' signals letters hidden across 'jet-set's elite'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: See in one Greek at Troy person laying siege

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in puts the see letter inside the old Greek's name

parts.note: Nestor was the aged Greek counsellor at the siege of Troy
v stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Picture one of the Greeks besieging Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: To invest a town, in old military language, is to besiege it.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a fortress is to surround and blockade it, so the besieger does exactly that.
